description:
Hi! We are working on developing a Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions. Our project aims to provide real-time vital signs tracking, AI-driven health risk assessment, and early warnings for astronauts during long-duration space missions.
​About Me/Us:
Passionate about space technology, software development, and biomedical engineering. We are looking to build an innovative solution that enhances astronaut safety and well-being.
summary: ORBIT Health OS is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and medical decision-support prototype designed for long-duration and deep-space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable. It brings health-related observations, crew check-ins, exercise and performance trends, and spacecraft-environment information into one interface. The system checks data quality, compares patterns with personal baselines, identifies persistent or critical changes, and presents explainable risk states with suggested next-step procedures. Its local-first design is intended to keep monitoring, alerts, records, and guidance available during communication outages, then synchronize queued information when connectivity returns. The prototype uses simulated operational readings and research datasets as evidence context; it is not a clinically validated medical device and does not diagnose or prescribe.
details:
ORBIT Health: Offline-First Astronaut Health Monitoring & Decision Support

What it does: On deep-space missions, communication with Earth can be delayed by up to ~20 minutes each way, or lost completely during solar events. ORBIT Health runs onboard, with no internet needed. It turns physiological, behavioral, exercise, and cabin-environment readings into early warnings, plain-language explanations, and approved countermeasure playbooks.

How it works: A transparent 6-stage hybrid risk engine:

Data QC and unit quarantine

Robust personal baseline (median/MAD, EWMA), frozen while any alert is active

Single-event critical overrides (radiation, CO2)

N-of-M persistence and CUSUM trend detection

Evidence fusion with a vigilance guard (low vigilance alone can never trigger RED)

A structured explanation: Required Action, What Changed, Why It Matters

It has 5 risk states: GREEN, AMBER, ORANGE, RED, and GRAY. Missing or untrusted data goes to GRAY, never to a false GREEN. A store-and-forward outbox keeps alerts during blackouts and syncs them later without duplicates.

Interface: A live crew switcher, 6 biometric KPI cards, an interactive anatomical body map, longitudinal charts with the personal baseline band, and a judge panel to run scenarios live (muscle degradation, a radiation event, CO2 plus SANS symptoms offline, sensor failure, and link cut/restore).

NASA grounding: OSDR studies OSD-684, OSD-816, OSD-939, and OSD-1010 (corrected from OSD-1018), plus the BRSMPT Campaign 1 Ares cognitive data (SRT, Running Memory, Matching To Sample). The studies are used for mechanism context and monitoring rationale only, not for diagnosis.

Tools: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite, React, Vite, Chart.js, GitHub, Vercel.

Creativity: Explainable rules instead of a black-box model. Ethical gamification that never penalizes symptom reporting. Visual design that does not depend on color alone.

Limitations: All thresholds are illustrative, and the system has not been reviewed by space-medicine specialists. It supports decisions and does not replace clinicians.

SI disclosure: AI tools were used for ideation, research, coding/debugging, writing, and design. See the SI selections and the repository README.
